question:
I'm trying to build a macro to be executed on dbt on-run-start that will create all necessary Databricks functions.

I have created the following macro that works fine

-- NAMES
{% macro region_filter_function() %}
    {{ return(target.catalog  ~ '.mart.region_filter') }}
{% endmacro %}

-- DEFINITIONS
{% macro create_udfs() %}

CREATE FUNCTION IF NOT EXISTS {{ region_filter_function() }}(region STRING)
RETURN IF(IS_ACCOUNT_GROUP_MEMBER('BI_USERS'), true, region in ('US','GB','DK'));

{% endmacro %}

The moment I try to add a new CREATE FUNCTION below the existing one I get an error:
enter image description here

I have tried:

  • have each Create in its own macro and then have macro1 call macro2

  • use set and run_query

I always have the same error.

Running both in databricks works fine.

I do not want to pollute the on_run_start with infinite macro calls.

Any ideas?
title: DBT: Running multiple Databricks DDL on run-start via macro
answer:
After a bit more search I found this ticket which explains why this happens and at the end also shows a workaround: https://github.com/databricks/dbt-databricks/issues/831

Basically idea is to ensure each command ends with ";", that all commands are captured with {% set ... %} and a macro that is able to run command by command using run_query.
